newsitem.title: USA: Dlr weaker, fights to hold 1.82 marks at U.S. noon.
newsitem.headline: Dlr weaker, fights to hold 1.82 marks at U.S. noon.

text.p: The dollar remained mired lower agaist the mark at midsession after heightened concerns of higher German interest rates sparked a merciless round of hedge fund selling, dealers said.
Multi-market weakness knocked dollar/yen from overnight highs earned amid the devaluation of Asian currencies and worsening Japanese economic fundamentals.

Dealers said the latest in the litany of German central banker hints at a willingness to accept higher rates by switching to a variable rate repo in the near term was the primary culprit behind early dollar chaos.
"People are now more adamant that we are probably going to a variable repo rate in Germany sooner than later," said John Gariano, vice president at Sumitomo Bank New York.

On Thursday, Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum fueled fears of higher rates as he reminded markets that the option of variable-rate repo tender remained open amid signs of rising inflation.

The dollar was quoted 1.8225/35 at midday from an early low of 1.8155 and 1.8355/59 at the open. It was lower versus the yen at 117.75/80 from 118.42/52 at the open, but well off the morning low of 116.82.
Dealers said the shift of sentiment surrounding future German interest rates has prompted consistent dollar/mark selling by large hedge funds and heavy liquidations in Europe.
"Hedge funds came in in early New York and we just ran into a whole bunch of stops at 1.8260 marks," said Chris Melendez, vice president and senior dealer at Sanwa Bank California.
A 2.3-percent slide in the German DAX-30 index to below the key 4,100 level also prompted managers to assess positions and the future of German interest rates, dealers said.
U.S. assets made the dollar's woes more uncomfortable, with the Dow industrials off more than 100 points and persistent weakness in U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.

The long bond retraced some losses at mid-morning after the University of Michigan said its preliminary read of consumer sentiment in August fell to 102.8 from 107.1 in July. The bond was trading off 13/32 in the early afternoon.

In dollar/yen, dealers said sudden losses were mostly a result of deep losses for asset markets and dollar/mark. Economic repercussions for Japan in the Asian currency crisis were seen as longer term liabilities for the yen.

"Japanese economic woes will keep interest rates there at historic lows," Gariano said. "Now they're projecting crazy numbers like 1.50 percent yields on the (10-year) JGBs over the next couple of months."
The key 182nd 10-year JGB yield fell to a record low yield of 2.065 percent on Friday from 2.075 percent on Thursday.
Mark/yen strength also lent some support to dollar/yen, dealers said, paving the way for a solid dollar/mark rebound to 117.79/84 in early afternoon trade from the low of 116.85.

Elsewhere, the dollar was weaker against the Swiss franc at 1.5050/60 from 1.5150/60 at the open. The British pound stronger at $1.6082/92 from $1.5992/02 and the dollar was stronger at Canadian $1.3900/05 from C$1.3890/95.
Dealers said the Catholic Assumption Day holiday in Europe kept trading extremely thin and exaggerated movements.
